newsitem.title: USA: N.J. officials predict $1.1 bln budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: N.J. officials predict $1.1 bln budget surplus.

text.p: Favorable economic trends will provide New Jersey with a $200 million budget cushion, raising the year-end surplus to $1.09 billion, according to the Office of Legislative Services.
It said increased economic activity reflected in the new statistics should increase personal and corporate income tax revenues by $200 million when the budget year ends June 30.
A revised report on revenues is due from the state Treasurer's office by April 1.
Last week, the state Labor Department added to the good news with the release of February unemployment statistics showing a decrease to 5.5 percent, a six-year low.

One cloud on the fiscal future for Gov. Christie Whitman is a bill working its way through the Legislature requiring felons to serve 85 percent of their prison sentences. Department of Corrections officials warn that building the required prison cells and staffing them will cost $2 billion over a decade.
The bill, supported by Gov. Christine Whitman, has passed the state Senate and cleared by the Assembly Public Safety Committee. It awaits a floor vote in the lower chamber.
